{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABXtrI5Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhBSCMI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 3, "title": "Implement the complete initial browser-playable MSX1 emulator in Rust and WebAssembly", "body": "## Problem

The repository currently contains collaboration guidance but no emulator application. We need one complete initial release—not a series of milestone-only deliverables—that emulates an MSX1 from a new Rust implementation, runs in a web browser through WebAssembly, and provides a usable BASIC environment without requiring access to a physical MSX.

A CPU-only library, a static UI mockup, or a build that cannot boot and run programs in the browser does **not** resolve this Issue.

## Expected outcome

Deliver an end-to-end, browser-playable **MSX1** emulator written from scratch in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly, with working video, keyboard/input, PSG audio, MSX1 ROM cartridges, and a BASIC prompt in which users can enter and run programs. Host a working public demo (prefer GitHub Pages) and document how to run and test it locally.

The emulator implementation must not copy code from an existing emulator. Public MSX hardware specifications, independently written tests, and properly attributed references may be used. Clearly separate the platform-independent Rust core from the minimal browser/Wasm interface.

A built-in BASIC boot path must use only code/ROMs that we author or have independently verified permission to redistribute under their licenses. Also support locally loading a user's own lawfully obtained original MSX BIOS/BASIC ROM where practical. Never commit or redistribute unlicensed proprietary BIOS, BASIC, game, or cartridge ROMs.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`, default branch `main`.
- At Issue creation, the repository has contributor/agent guidance, Issue/PR templates, and no application build or test commands.
- Target: initial **MSX1** compatibility. MSX2/MSX2+, disk drives, tape support, MegaROM mappers, and advanced peripherals are outside the required initial scope unless necessary for the demonstrable MSX1 scenarios below.
- Browser delivery is part of the product, not an optional follow-up. Browser restrictions on audio playback and local file access must be handled appropriately.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Rust emulator and MSX1 hardware

- [ ] Create a buildable Rust project with a platform-independent emulator core and appropriate tests, plus a WebAssembly/browser entry point; document actual development, build, and validation commands.
- [ ] Implement Z80 CPU registers, flags, instruction decoding/execution (including documented prefix instruction families), memory and I/O operations, stack, reset/HALT, interrupt modes, IRQ/NMI, and instruction timing sufficiently accurate to boot BASIC and run the acceptance software; validate with deterministic CPU tests and documented test vectors.
- [ ] Implement the MSX1 memory map and primary-slot selection, RAM, BIOS/BASIC and cartridge ROM mappings, relevant I/O ports, the PPI and keyboard matrix, and boot/reset behavior.
- [ ] Implement the MSX1 TMS9918A-compatible VDP, including VRAM, registers/status, display modes needed by MSX1 BASIC, text/tiles, sprites, frame rendering, and VBlank interrupt behavior; render correctly to the browser's Canvas or equivalent.
- [ ] Implement the AY-3-8910-compatible PSG and the MSX1 input/I/O integration; make audible output work in the browser via Web Audio (accounting for the required user interaction to unlock audio).
- [ ] Support loading a standard MSX1 ROM cartridge through a browser file picker, with correct slot mapping and reset/boot behavior. Use redistributable/self-authored test ROMs for automated verification rather than bundling copyrighted games.

### BASIC and legally redistributable boot

- [ ] Provide a **usable BASIC prompt directly in the browser without a user-supplied proprietary ROM**, using a self-authored or explicitly redistributable BIOS/BASIC implementation with source, provenance, and license requirements documented. Do not misrepresent a boot stub or C-BIOS alone as a complete BASIC interpreter.
- [ ] In that BASIC environment, users can type, edit, list, and run a numbered program, and basic constructs work end to end (at minimum `PRINT`, variable assignment, `IF/THEN`, `GOTO`, `FOR/NEXT`, `LIST`, and `RUN`). Clearly document any limitations compared with original MSX BASIC.
- [ ] Where practical, provide a local-only file-loading path for a user-supplied MSX1 system ROM (BIOS/BASIC), without uploading the ROM to a server; do not distribute the original proprietary ROM.
- [ ] Document licenses and attribution for every bundled ROM/asset, and ensure the repo and deployable build contain no ROMs without established redistribution rights.

### Browser integration and end-to-end operation

- [ ] Compile and run the emulator as Wasm in a current desktop browser, with visible MSX video, interactive keyboard input, working emulation/frame pacing, start/reset controls, ROM selection, and audio enablement.
- [ ] Supply local build/run instructions and a reproducible browser smoke-test flow (manual steps are acceptable only where browser automation cannot reliably cover the interaction). Check the actual rendered application rather than only whether Wasm compiles.
- [ ] Demonstrate and verify in the running browser: boot to BASIC; type and run `10 FOR I=1 TO 5 : PRINT I : NEXT I` (or an equivalent multi-line program) with correct visible output; run a graphics/VDP test; hear a PSG tone after activating audio; load and execute a redistributable MSX1 test cartridge.
- [ ] Include reproducible Rust and browser-level verification appropriate to the actual implementation, and record commands, results, limitations, and any skipped checks in the PR. Do not claim success based only on a passing build.
- [ ] Add the static browser deployment configuration needed to publish a playable demo, preferably with GitHub Pages, and verify its configuration/build artifacts before merge. A local-only development server is not the final deliverable.
- [ ] Update the README with project overview, supported features/known limitations, local build/test/run instructions, ROM/legal guidance, and the demo URL or clearly identified target URL.
- [ ] Keep the change within the initial playable MSX1 goal: no unrelated framework, policy, or speculative feature work. Follow the repository's English Issue/PR documentation and Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge flow.

## Optional validation

- Compare behavior against an MSX1 reference emulator and, later, physical MSX hardware.
- Test extra third-party game cartridges provided by their rights holders or with redistribution permission.
- Try additional browsers and mobile devices beyond the primary desktop-browser smoke test.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After merge, verify the published demo URL actually loads the Wasm build and boots to an interactive BASIC prompt, and that keyboard interaction, ROM-file selection, and audio activation work as described. Record the real URL and outcome; if the hosting service requires one-time repository configuration, identify that prerequisite explicitly rather than claiming deployment succeeded from pre-merge checks alone.
